circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke and home to Formula One's season-concluding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain and preceding circuits built in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street-based motorsport venue in Melbourne that encircles Albert Park Lake. Hosting the Australian Grand Prix annually along with various support categories, the track holds FIA Grade 1 certification and serves as a premier venue for Formula One racing in Australia.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the home of the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. After undergoing reconstruction and shortening, the track was renamed and returned to hosting the Austrian Grand Prix during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital that stretches 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One racing. The circuit first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016, before being renamed to host the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Located in Bahrain and spanning 5. 412 km, this FIA Grade 1 circuit has hosted the Formula One Grand Prix annually since 2004, marking the championship's inaugural Middle Eastern venue. Beyond Formula One, the facility accommodates various motorsport categories including GP2 racing, drag racing, and 24-hour endurance competitions, with multiple circuit configurations available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced layout combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for competing teams. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated in the Walloon region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has been hosting the Belgian Grand Prix since 1925 and participated in Formula One's inaugural season in 1950. The venue has maintained an annual Grand Prix presence since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: The Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometre track located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, and serves as the home of the FIA Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond hosting Formula One, the venue has accommodated various other motorsport series including sports car championships, open-wheel racing, and NASCAR competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit, located in Shanghai's Jiading District, is a motorsport venue primarily recognized for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which took place annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track has expanded its racing calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, this English circuit inaugurated the British Grand Prix in 1948 and later hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After alternating with two other venues between 1955 and 1986, the championship event became a permanent fixture at the track from 1987 onwards, while the circuit also serves as a regular stop on the MotoGP calendar.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: Located near Budapest in Mogyoród, the Hungaroring is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it opened in 1986. Built in just eight months, a faster construction period than any other Formula One track, the venue was established near a major highway after plans for a street circuit in the capital's largest park were rejected by the government.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza, located near Milan in northern Italy, is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing facility. It hosts the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, earning the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its notably long straightaways and quick corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km motorsport venue in Mie Prefecture, Japan, operated by a Honda subsidiary and hosting approximately 155,000 spectators. The track gained prominence as a major Formula One Grand Prix destination and serves as a key event in both international and Japanese motorsport championships.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, following portions of the famous Las Vegas Boulevard lined with major casinos and hotels. The track weaves past iconic landmarks such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a unique urban racing environment centered around the entertainment district.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit named after two tragic racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who died in separate accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The track has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix since 2015 on its current layout, resuming a tradition that previously ran during two earlier periods before ending in 1992, with the event now branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix from 2021 onwards.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One racing, the venue was integrated into the championship calendar beginning in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a compact 3. 337 km street layout winding through Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, circling the harbour of this principality. Though officially named after the circuit itself, it is widely known as Monte Carlo due to the race's predominant coverage of that neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes northwest of Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix upon its return to Formula One in 2021 after a lengthy absence. The partnership between the venue and Formula One concluded in 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit, situated near Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419 km track featuring a lengthy 1. 068 km main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, this 4. 309 km Brazilian circuit opened in 1940 and received its current name in 1985 as a tribute to deceased Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace. The anticlockwise layout has hosted numerous grand prix events at this historically significant venue, which also features a karting facility bearing another famous Brazilian racing driver's name.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront. Since its introduction to the Formula One calendar in 2021, it has served as the home of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, while also hosting the Formula E championship from 2025 onward.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through the heart of Singapore's waterfront, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang districts into its racing layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, situated near Barcelona in Catalonia, measures 4. 657 kilometers and features a diverse mix of straights and corners that make it suitable for testing multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the venue for the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside various other motorsport competitions including NASCAR and MotoGP events. The track has hosted numerous racing series throughout its history, ranging from endurance racing championships to rallycross and open-wheel competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver who represents Thailand in Formula One while driving for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having claimed two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 along with 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved significant success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both F1 and sportscar world titles.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli began his Formula One career in 2025 with Mercedes, where he currently competes. He has already secured seven Grand Prix victories during his time in the sport.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, where he competes in the sport's top motorseries.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One with the Audi team, bringing his motorsport expertise to the sport's premier championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing experience from a lengthy career spanning over a decade. The two-time championship runner-up achieved his podium finishes while racing for Mercedes, where he also claimed 10 race victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Alejandro Colapinto currently races in Formula One as a member of the Alpine team. He has established himself as a competitor in the sport's premier racing category.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan holds a reserve position with Haas while pursuing his professional racing interests in European prototype competition. He has made limited Formula One appearances, featuring in seven races across the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly represents France in Formula One racing with Alpine. The driver achieved a significant career milestone by securing victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian racing driver competing for Red Bull Racing in Formula One under the French flag.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has achieved seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple racing records including the most career victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One while having achieved significant success in endurance motorsport, notably claiming victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 alongside Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver competes for Ferrari in Formula One, having achieved nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning nine seasons. Leclerc finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while driving for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish racing driver who previously competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. Currently, he drives for BMW as a factory driver in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT, while also pursuing a part-time career in NASCAR's top series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British driver competing for McLaren in Formula One, having claimed the 2025 World Drivers' Championship with the team. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: French driver Esteban Ocon currently races for Haas in Formula One. He previously secured a Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian round while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio "Checo" Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from over a decade and a half in the sport. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has claimed six race victories throughout his F1 career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, where he has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories during his tenure spanning four seasons.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One from 2011 through 2024 and claimed eight Grand Prix victories during his 14-season career.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured seven race victories throughout his eight-year career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz has established himself as a consistent competitor across 12 Formula One seasons, securing four Grand Prix victories. He currently races for Williams in the championship.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously campaigned in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin in the sport's premier championship series.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, holds a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. After competing as a full-time driver from 2021 through 2025, he transitioned to a reserve role in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024, along with 71 Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season Formula One career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver currently employed as a reserve driver for Cadillac in Formula One. He competed in the sport's top category from 2022 through 2024 and holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese driver to have raced in Formula One.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based outfit rebranded as Alpine in 2021 to represent Renault's sports car marque while maintaining its status as the French manufacturer's works team. Previously operating under the Renault F1 Team name, Alpine competed in the championship until Renault's withdrawal at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has competed in Formula One through multiple team structures, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco racing banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's longest-surviving and most accomplished team, fielding entries continuously since the championship's 1950 inception. The squad, colloquially dubbed the Prancing Horse for its iconic emblem, remains a foundational pillar of the sport's history and competitive landscape.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed F1 team founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas, the outfit commenced racing in 2016 after its establishment in 2014. Currently led by team principal Ayao Komatsu following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, the squad has competed throughout the modern era of the sport.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering and racing enterprise founded by Peter Sauber in 1970, the outfit initially built sports cars before transitioning to Formula One machinery as an independent manufacturer. Following success in endurance competition, including a Le Mans 24 Hours victory in 1989, the team competed in F1 from 1993 until 2025, becoming one of the sport's longest-serving constructors before its acquisition by Audi to establish the foundation for Audi's own F1 program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited operates as a British Formula One team headquartered in Woking, Surrey, and is part of the McLaren Group, which is fully owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One as both constructor and power unit supplier since 1954, with its current iteration based in Brackley operating under a German licence. The team, now jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff following a 2022 restructuring, competes as Mercedes-AMG Petronas and carries the historic "Silver Arrows" designation associated with Mercedes racing heritage.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team structure alongside Red Bull Racing. Operating from Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the team functions as Red Bull's sister squad within the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024 as Red Bull GmbH's second team. Based in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, it operates alongside the primary Red Bull Racing outfit within the Red Bull group's two-team structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing competes in Formula One under an Austrian licence while operating from England, representing one of two teams owned by Red Bull GmbH. Founded in 2005 and led by Christian Horner for two decades, the team transitioned to Laurent Mekies as team principal in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering stands as a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's previous unsuccessful racing venture. Operating from their Grove, Oxfordshire headquarters, the team competes in the championship as Atlassian Williams F1 Team.
